rules.name: Switching Behavior

constraint.value: Switches must forward frames based on MAC addresses and Virtual Link identifiers.

rules.source_quote: 2.6 Switching
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can send frames with incorrect or non-existent MAC addresses or Virtual Link identifiers to test if switches forward them improperly.

rules.name: System Performance Requirements

constraint.value: The network must meet specific performance criteria including latency, jitter, and throughput.

rules.source_quote: 2.7 System Performance
rules.test_hint: Fuzzer can generate traffic patterns that exceed expected network load to test if performance criteria are violated.

rules.name: Frame Filtering

constraint.value: Frames must be filtered based on predefined criteria to ensure only valid frames are forwarded.

rules.source_quote: 4.1.1.2 Frame Filtering
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with invalid headers or payloads to test if they are correctly filtered out by the switch.

rules.name: Traffic Policing

constraint.value: Traffic must be policed to ensure compliance with bandwidth and transmission constraints.

rules.source_quote: 4.1.1.3 Traffic Policing
rules.test_hint: Send traffic exceeding the allowed bandwidth to test if the switch enforces policing rules.

rules.name: Frame Filtering Function

constraint.value: Frames must be filtered based on predefined criteria before being processed further.

rules.source_quote: 4.2.1 Frame Filtering
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that do not meet the filtering criteria and observe if they are correctly discarded.

rules.name: Traffic Policing Function

constraint.value: Traffic must be policed to ensure compliance with bandwidth and priority constraints.

rules.source_quote: 4.2.2 Traffic Policing
rules.test_hint: Send traffic that exceeds bandwidth limits and check if it is appropriately policed.

rules.name: Switching Function

constraint.value: Switches must forward frames based on virtual link identifiers.

rules.source_quote: 4.4 Switching Function
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect virtual link identifiers and verify if they are not forwarded.

rules.name: Addressing Policy

constraint.value: End systems must adhere to the addressing policy for frame transmission.

rules.source_quote: 4.5.2 Addressing Policy
rules.test_hint: Transmit frames with incorrect addressing and observe if they are rejected.

rules.name: Interoperable Functional Elements
rules.source_quote: The requirements listed in this document aim at specifying interoperable functional elements: Data link: MAC, VL addressing concept; Network: IP, ICMP; Transport: UDP, TCP (optional); Network application layers: Sampling, Queuing, SAP, TFTP and SNMP.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic using unsupported protocols to test if the network rejects or mishandles them.

rules.name: Physical Layer Compatibility

constraint.value: Must be compatible with ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.

rules.source_quote: Physical layer is not specified here, but should be any of the ARINC 664 Part 2 defined solutions.

rules.name: Switch Interchangeability

constraint.value: Any AFDX compliant switch can be connected to any AFDX network if Form and Fit requirements are respected.

rules.source_quote: This means that any AFDX compliant LRU (including switch) can be connected to any AFDX network, as far as the Form and Fit requirements (specific to the System and not specified in this document) are respected.

rules.name: Deterministic Network Communication

constraint.value: The AFDX network must ensure deterministic communication, allowing communication with a wider profiled network through routers or gateways.

rules.source_quote: The AFDX network is a special case of a profiled network. A deterministic network may communicate with a wider profiled network and by inference, with a compliant network through routers or gateways.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a scenario where the network does not maintain deterministic communication, and observe if the network can still interface correctly with wider networks.

rules.name: Timely Delivery of Data

constraint.value: The network must ensure timely delivery of data, which is critical for quality of service.

rules.source_quote: Part 7 describes a subset of this network, where quality of service including timely delivery is paramount.
rules.test_hint: Introduce delays in data transmission and observe if the network maintains quality of service by ensuring timely delivery.

rules.name: Real-Time Communication Links

constraint.value: The network must provide reliable real-time communication links for safety-critical systems.

rules.source_quote: For safety critical systems reliable “real time” communication links are essential.
rules.test_hint: Test the network's ability to maintain real-time communication under varying loads and conditions to ensure reliability.

rules.name: Total Latency Calculation

constraint.value: L = Ts + Tm + Tr

rules.source_quote: and the total latency, L, is :  L = Ts + Tm + Tr

rules.name: Jitter Time Calculation

constraint.value: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap

rules.source_quote: Simultaneous reception of frames from ESa and ESb at the switch will be dealt with by sequencing the two frames for re-transmission to ES c, with a maximum jitter dependent on the message length: Tj = (8 x M) / Nbw + Tmin_gap
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with varying sizes (M) and observe the jitter time (Tj) to ensure it follows the formula.

rules.name: Latency for First Frame

constraint.value: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + (8 x M)/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr

rules.source_quote: Latency for the first frame: La = Ts + Tm1 + Tsw + ( 8 x M )/Nbw + Tm2 + Tr
rules.test_hint: Send a single frame and measure the latency to ensure it matches the calculated La.

rules.name: Latency for Delayed Frame

constraint.value: Lb = La + Tj

rules.source_quote: Latency for the delayed frame: Lb = La + Tj
rules.test_hint: Send multiple frames and measure the latency of the delayed frame to ensure it matches the calculated Lb.

rules.name: Frame Sequencing in Switch

constraint.value: Frames are sequenced for re-transmission with a maximum jitter dependent on message length.

rules.source_quote: Simultaneous reception of frames from ESa and ESb at the switch will be dealt with by sequencing the two frames for re-transmission to ES c, with a maximum jitter dependent on the message length
rules.test_hint: Send frames simultaneously from different sources and verify that the switch sequences them correctly with the expected jitter.

rules.name: Continued Delivery in Fault Conditions
rules.source_quote: For the system to maintain maximum integrity in the event of a fault on either ESa or ESb, the Quality of Service (QoS) definition may include continued delivery of data from the non-faulty node.
rules.test_hint: Introduce a fault in one end system and verify that data continues to be delivered from the non-faulty node.

rules.name: Maximum Bandwidth Allocation

constraint.value: Lmax/TGAP

rules.source_quote: The maximum bandwidth allocated to this VL is: Lmax/TGAP.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic that exceeds the calculated maximum bandwidth for a VL to test if the network enforces this limit.

rules.name: Bounded Arrival Distribution

constraint.value: Frame delivery follows a bounded arrival distribution.

rules.source_quote: In an AFDX network, the analysis also assumes that the transmitting end-systems are not synchronized, but that frame delivery follows a bounded arrival distribution.
rules.test_hint: Introduce unsynchronized frame deliveries to test if the network can maintain bounded arrival distribution.

rules.name: Maximum Latency Calculation

constraint.value: Maximum latency is calculable.

rules.source_quote: This results in a calculable maximum latency in the network, rather than a probabilistic latency.

rules.name: Ordinal Integrity of Frames
rules.source_quote: For this reason AFDX requires ordinal integrity of frames within a Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Send frames out of order within a VL to test if the network maintains ordinal integrity.

rules.name: Guaranteed Service Class
rules.source_quote: Therefore, the only service class needed in the Aircraft Network is a guaranteed service.

rules.name: Guaranteed Bandwidth and Latency

constraint.value: Bandwidth and bounded latency are guaranteed.

rules.source_quote: To summarise, a guaranteed service leads to the following characteristics: • Bandwidth and bounded latency are guaranteed
rules.test_hint: Introduce traffic that attempts to exceed the guaranteed bandwidth or latency to test if the network maintains these guarantees.

rules.name: Single Source per Virtual Link

constraint.value: Only one End System within the Avionics network should be the source of any one VL.

rules.source_quote: Only one End System within the Avionics network should be the source of any one VL.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure multiple End Systems as sources for the same Virtual Link and observe if the network enforces the single source rule.

rules.name: Dedicated Maximum Bandwidth

constraint.value: Each Virtual Link has a dedicated maximum bandwidth allocated by the System Integrator.

rules.source_quote: Each Virtual Link has a dedicated maximum bandwidth. This bandwidth is allocated by the System Integrator.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to exceed the allocated bandwidth for a Virtual Link and observe if the network enforces the bandwidth limit.

rules.name: Logical Isolation of Bandwidth

constraint.value: The ES should provide logical isolation with respect to available bandwidth among the Virtual Link(s) it supports.

rules.source_quote: The ES should provide logical isolation with respect to available bandwidth among the Virtual Link(s) it supports.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to affect the bandwidth of one Virtual Link by altering the traffic on another and observe if the network maintains isolation.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap
rules.source_quote: The Traffic shaping function of the ES should be able to handle BAG values in range 1 ms to 128 ms. These values should satisfy the following formula: BAG=2k [in ms], (k integer in range 0 to 7).
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use a BAG value outside the specified range or not conforming to the formula and observe if the network rejects it.

rules.name: Maximum Frame Size
rules.source_quote: The End System should accommodate VL frames up to a size of 1518 bytes in both transmission and reception.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send or receive frames larger than 1518 bytes and observe if the network rejects them.

rules.name: Maximum Admissible Jitter

constraint.value: 0 < Jitter < MaxBAG

rules.source_quote: At the output of the scheduler, for a given Virtual Link, frames can appear in a bounded time interval. This interval is defined as the maximum admissible jitter.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to introduce jitter beyond the maximum admissible limit and observe if the network detects or corrects it.

rules.name: Maximum Transmission Latency
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the end-system in transmission should be bounded and lower than 150 μs + frame delay.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic with excessive processing delays to exceed the 150 μs technological latency.

rules.name: Maximum Reception Latency
rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the end-system in reception should be bounded and lower than 150 μs.
rules.test_hint: Introduce delays in processing incoming frames to exceed the 150 μs technological latency.

rules.name: Full Frame Rate Processing

constraint.value: Process received frames at full frame rate of the medium

rules.source_quote: To avoid losing incoming frames during a burst, and to fix the IFG in transmission, the MAC layer of the end-system should be able to: Process received frames at full frame rate of the medium...
rules.test_hint: Send frames at maximum rate and check if the end system can process them without loss.

rules.name: Back-to-Back Frame Transmission

constraint.value: Transmit frames back to back

rules.source_quote: To avoid losing incoming frames during a burst, and to fix the IFG in transmission, the MAC layer of the end-system should be able to: Transmit frames back to back
rules.test_hint: Attempt to transmit frames with minimal inter-frame gap and verify compliance.

rules.name: Maximum Jitter
rules.source_quote: In all cases, the jitter is bounded at 500μs to limit the impact on determinism for the whole network.
rules.test_hint: Introduce variable delays in frame transmission to exceed the 500 μs jitter limit.

rules.name: Maximum Latency for Single Frame

constraint.value: MAX_Latency_i ≤ BAG_i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission

rules.source_quote: the total allowed latency for a given VLi is: MAX_Latency i ≤ BAG i + Max_jitter + Technological_Latency_in_transmission
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with latency exceeding the calculated maximum to test system response.

rules.name: MAC Destination Address Format

constraint.value: xxxx xx11 xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx

rules.source_quote: A MAC destination address in the AFDX frame should be a Group and Locally Administered address and should be compliant with the following format. 48 bits Constant field 32 bits Virtual Link Identifier 16 bits xxxx xx11 xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx
rules.test_hint: Use a MAC destination address that does not comply with the specified format to test system handling.

rules.name: MAC Source Address Format
rules.source_quote: The Constant field is set to “0000 0010 0000 0000 0000 0000” as shown in Figure 3-11. The least significant bit of the first byte indicates the Individual Address = 0. The second to least significant bit of the first byte indicates the locally administered address = 1.
rules.test_hint: Use a MAC source address that does not comply with the specified format to test system handling.

rules.name: Interface ID Definition
rules.source_quote: The Interface_ID, defined in Figure 3-12, indicates to which redundant AFDX network(s) the Ethernet MAC controller is connected. 0 0 1 The Ethernet MAC controller is connected to the network A 0 1 0 The Ethernet MAC controller is connected to the network B
rules.test_hint: Use an Interface_ID value outside the allowed set to test system response.

rules.name: Sequence Number Addition
rules.source_quote: Per VL, the End System should add a sequence number for each transmitted frame on the AFDX network. The frame sequence number should be one octet long with a range of 0 to 255.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames without sequence numbers or with sequence numbers outside the 0-255 range.

rules.name: First Valid Wins Policy

constraint.value: first frame with the next valid sequence number is accepted; duplicates are discarded

rules.source_quote: In default mode each frame is sent across both of two networks. Upon reception, an algorithm in the communications stack (below IP layer) uses a 'First Valid wins' policy.
rules.test_hint: Send duplicate frames and check if the second one is incorrectly processed.

rules.name: Sequence Number Location

constraint.value: The frame sequence number should be located just before the MAC CRC field, as part of the MAC payload.

rules.source_quote: The frame sequence number should be located just before the MAC CRC field, as part of the MAC payload, as illustrated in Figure 3-19.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with the sequence number located incorrectly to test if the network rejects them.

rules.name: Redundant Frame Timing
rules.source_quote: In order to simplify the algorithm on the receiving End System, redundant copies of a frame should be sent within a maximum time difference of 0.5 ms.
rules.test_hint: Send redundant frames with a time difference greater than 0.5 ms to test if the network detects and flags them.

rules.name: Sequence Number Range

constraint.value: [PSN+1, PSN+2]

rules.source_quote: For each network the Integrity Checking tests each frame for a sequence number in the interval: [PSN”+”1,PSN”+”2]
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sequence numbers outside the valid range to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: SkewMax Parameter

constraint.value: The SkewMax value should be provided by the system integrator and is based on network topology.

rules.source_quote: RM configuration is generally based on the SkewMax parameter: i.e. the maximum time between the reception of two redundant frames.

rules.name: First Win Redundancy

constraint.value: Deliver the first of the redundant frames received

rules.source_quote: When redundancy management is active, it should deliver the first of the redundant frames received.
rules.test_hint: Send multiple redundant frames and check if only the first one is processed.

rules.name: Reset Resilience
rules.source_quote: Reset of any equipment involved in the communication (transmitting End system, receiving End system or the AFDX switch) should not affect this property.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a reset and verify that redundancy management continues to deliver the first frame.

rules.name: Increasing RSN Order

constraint.value: Frames must be forwarded in an increasing RSN order

rules.source_quote: For each VL at the receiver, the Redundancy Management (RM) function should ensure that frames are forwarded in an increasing RSN order.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with non-increasing RSN and check if they are rejected or reordered.

rules.name: SkewMax Handling

constraint.value: If skew max is exceeded, accept the next frame regardless of sequence number

rules.source_quote: If skew max is exceeded after the reception of a frame, RM will accept the next frame whatever its sequence number is.
rules.test_hint: Exceed SkewMax and send a frame with an out-of-order sequence number to see if it is accepted.

rules.name: In-sequence Forwarding

constraint.value: Forward only in-sequence frames

rules.source_quote: The Redundancy Management function must forward only in-sequence frames, but reordering is not required.
rules.test_hint: Send out-of-sequence frames and verify they are not forwarded.

rules.name: Port Sharing Restriction
rules.source_quote: A user port is configured to either transmit or receive, but not both.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure a user port to both transmit and receive simultaneously.

rules.name: Sampling Com Port IP Fragmentation

constraint.value: less than or equal to the payload size of the associated Virtual Link

rules.source_quote: Sampling Com Ports should not use IP fragmentation, therefore the size of each sampling message should be less than or equal to the payload size of the associated Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Send a sampling message that exceeds the payload size of the associated Virtual Link to test for fragmentation handling.

rules.name: Sampling Service Communication Type
rules.source_quote: Sampling service should be based on multicast and unidirectional communication to send data from one source to one or several receptors.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use a non-multicast or bidirectional communication method for sampling services.

rules.name: Queuing Service Message Size Management

constraint.value: manage messages of different sizes

rules.source_quote: The queuing service should be able to manage messages of different sizes for the same queuing Communication Port.
rules.test_hint: Send messages of varying sizes through the same queuing Communication Port to test size management.

rules.name: Queuing Service FIFO Discipline

constraint.value: FIFO discipline in transmission and reception

rules.source_quote: To guarantee the sequence of messages, the queuing service should manage the messages with FIFO discipline in transmission and reception.
rules.test_hint: Send messages in a specific order and verify that they are received in the same order.

rules.name: Queuing Service Data Capacity

constraint.value: up to 8192

rules.source_quote: Each instance of Queuing Service should be able to manage up to 8 k octets of application data (IP fragmentation is thus needed).
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send more than 8192 octets of data through a single instance of the Queuing Service.

rules.name: Fragmentation Order

constraint.value: fragments should be transmitted in-order

rules.source_quote: When fragmentation is used, the fragments should be transmitted in-order to the AFDX network.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented messages and verify that fragments are transmitted in the correct order.

rules.name: Buffer Overflow Handling

constraint.value: send error indication and discard frame

rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in transmission, an error indication should be sent to the transmitting partition and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a buffer overflow condition and check if an error indication is sent and the frame is discarded.

rules.name: Complete message reassembly before presentation

constraint.value: No data should be presented to a partition until the whole message has been reassembled

rules.source_quote: In case of fragmentation, no data should be presented to a partition in the queuing services FIFO until whole message has been reassembled.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented frames and check if the network presents incomplete messages to partitions.

rules.name: Buffer overflow handling

constraint.value: If a buffer overflow occurs in reception, an error message should be sent to the receiving partition and the frame should be discarded.

rules.source_quote: If a buffer overflow occurs in reception, an error message should be sent to the receiving partition and the frame should be discarded.
rules.test_hint: Intentionally cause buffer overflow and verify if an error message is sent and the frame is discarded.

rules.name: UDP Service Access Point octet limit
rules.source_quote: Each instance of the UDP Service Access Point should handle up to 8k octets.
rules.test_hint: Send UDP packets exceeding 8k octets and observe if they are handled correctly.

rules.name: VL FIFO queue Sub-VL limit

constraint.value: 0 to 4

rules.source_quote: A VL FIFO queue should be able to manage at most 4 Sub-VL FIFO queues.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure more than 4 Sub-VL FIFO queues and observe if the system enforces the limit.

rules.name: Round robin sequence for Sub-VL FIFO queues

constraint.value: Each Sub-VL FIFO queue should be read in round-robin sequence such that if any Sub-VL FIFO queue has traffic, one frame per BAG is sent to the main VL.

rules.source_quote: Each Sub-VF FIFO queue should be read in round-robin sequence such that if any Sub-VF FIFO queue has traffic, one frame per BAG is sent to the main VL.
rules.test_hint: Check if the Sub-VL FIFO queues are read in a round-robin manner by sending traffic to multiple Sub-VLs and observing the order of frame transmission.

rules.name: Ethernet Frame Compliance

constraint.value: Frames must comply with IEEE 802.3 standard

rules.source_quote: Any Ethernet Frame generated by the End System should be compliant with IEEE 802.3 standard.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames that do not comply with IEEE 802.3 to test compliance enforcement.

rules.name: Transmission Continuity on Link Failure

constraint.value: true

rules.source_quote: All output interfaces will continue to transmit, even in the case of a physical layer link failure.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a link failure and check if transmission continues.

rules.name: Maximum AFDX Frame Length

constraint.value: Defined per VL

rules.source_quote: A maximum AFDX frame length should be defined on a per VL basis.
rules.test_hint: Send frames exceeding the maximum length defined for a VL to test enforcement.

rules.name: IPv4 Packet Structure Compliance

constraint.value: Packets must comply with Figure 3-30

rules.source_quote: IPv4 packet structure should be compliant with Figure 3-30.
rules.test_hint: Generate packets that do not comply with the specified structure to test compliance.

rules.name: IPv4 Total Length Field Range
rules.source_quote: Ordinarily, in the IPv4 packet structure, the Total Length field should range from 21 to 1500 bytes. In AFDX, this range is from 21 to 1499 due to the Sequence Number.
rules.test_hint: Send packets with Total Length outside the range [21, 1499] to test enforcement.

rules.name: Frame Forwarding on Validity

constraint.value: Forward frames if FCS and CRC are valid

rules.source_quote: In reception, if the AFDX frame format and Frame Check Sequence (FCS) and Cyclic Redundancy Check (CRC) are valid (without preamble and Start Frame Delimiter fields) the frame should be forwarded to the upper layer.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with invalid FCS or CRC to test if they are correctly not forwarded.

rules.name: Unique Message Identification

constraint.value: Each message in the AFDX network is uniquely identified by a quintuplet consisting of UDP Source Port, Source IP, Destination MAC, Destination IP, and UDP Destination Port.

rules.source_quote: In the AFDX network, this quintuplet provides a unique identification for each message.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could attempt to send frames with non-unique quintuplets to test if the network correctly identifies and handles them.

rules.name: Static Addressing for Intra-AFDX

constraint.value: For Intra-AFDX communication, the addressing for each message is statically defined.

rules.source_quote: The principal characteristic of Intra-AFDX communication is the fact that for each message, the addressing is statically defined.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could attempt to send frames with dynamic or incorrect addressing to test if the network enforces static addressing.

rules.name: Bi-directional Communication Ports

constraint.value: Bi-directional communication at a single ES requires two AFDX communication ports: one transmitter and one receiver.

rules.source_quote: Bi-directional communication, at a single ES should require two AFDX communication ports: one transmitter and one receiver.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could attempt to use a single port for bi-directional communication to test if the network enforces the requirement for separate transmitter and receiver ports.

rules.name: IP Source Address Format

constraint.value: Class A, Private Internet Unicast Address, First 8 bits '0000 1010'

rules.source_quote: The IP address should be Class A and private Internet Unicast Address (First 8 bits should be ‘0000 1010’).
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with incorrect IP source address format, such as using a non-Class A address or incorrect first 8 bits.

rules.name: IP Destination Address Format

value: IP Multicast address compliant to format

rules.source_quote: The IP destination address in the IP header of the AFDX frame should be: Either the IP Unicast address to identify the target subscriber Or an IP Multicast address compliant to the format shown in Figure 3-38
rules.test_hint: Send frames with destination addresses that are neither valid unicast nor compliant multicast addresses.

rules.name: AFDX Communication Port Unidirectional Link

constraint.value: In transmission, link to a single set of UDP port source, IP source, VL (MAC destination), IP destination, and UDP destination.

rules.source_quote: In transmission, an AFDX Communication Port should only be linked to a single set UDP port source, IP source, VL (MAC destination), IP destination and UDP destination.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure an AFDX Communication Port to link to multiple sets of parameters in transmission.

rules.name: Unique SAP Port Linkage in Transmission

constraint.value: A SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP port source, IP source, and VL (MAC destination)) in transmission.

rules.source_quote: In transmission, a SAP Port should only be linked to a single set (UDP port source, IP source and VL (MAC destination)).
rules.test_hint: Attempt to link a SAP Port to multiple sets in transmission and observe if the network rejects this configuration.

rules.name: Service Access Point Identification

constraint.value: The UDP/TCP port number should identify the Service Access Point.

rules.source_quote: The UDP/TCP port number should identify the Service Access Point.

rules.name: Port Number Allocation Range
rules.source_quote: Port range (decimal value) Allocation range ARINC 664 Allocation range AFDX 0 – 1023 Administered by ICANN 'Well-known' port number Administered by ICANN 'Well-known' port number 1 024 – 16 383 Registered by ICANN A664 assigned 16 384 – 32 767 Registered by ICANN System integrator Or User defined 32 768 – 65 535 Registered by ICANN Recommended for temporary port assignment Assigned by network manager
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use port numbers outside the specified range and observe if the network rejects them.

rules.name: Port Number Uniqueness within a Virtual Link

constraint.value: Two identical port numbers cannot be used within a Virtual Link.

rules.source_quote: Port number duplication: the only technical limitation regarding port number duplication is that two identical port number cannot be used with in a Virtual Link.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use duplicate port numbers within a single Virtual Link and observe if the network rejects them.

rules.name: Maximum Frame Size
rules.source_quote: The maximum frame size for VLi is denoted S i max (expressed in bytes). S i max is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than 1538 bytes to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Minimum Frame Size
rules.source_quote: The minimum frame size for VLi is denoted S i min (expressed in bytes). S i min is a configurable parameter that should be in the range [84, 1538]. S i min should be less than or equal to S i max
rules.test_hint: Send frames smaller than 84 bytes to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence Validity

constraint.value: FCS embedded in the frame must match the calculation upon reception

rules.source_quote: The frame integrity: whether the FCS embedded in the frame matches the calculation upon reception
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect FCS to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Destination Address Validity

constraint.value: Destination Address must correspond to a valid VL

rules.source_quote: The frame path: whether the destination requested by the content of the Destination Address field (which in case of the AFDX is the Virtual Link Identifier) of the arriving frame is permitted or not
rules.test_hint: Send frames with invalid destination addresses to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Byte-Based Traffic Policing

constraint.value: Filters out VL in terms of bandwidth usage expressed in bits per second

rules.source_quote: The byte-based traffic policing filters out the VL in terms of bandwidth usage expressed in bits per second
rules.test_hint: Send traffic exceeding the bandwidth limit in bits per second to test if it is discarded.

rules.name: Byte-based Frame Acceptance

constraint.value: If Byte ACi is greater than S, the frame is accepted and Byte ACi is debited by S

rules.source_quote: If Byte ACi is greater than S, the frame is accepted and Byte ACi is debited by S
rules.test_hint: Send frames with varying sizes to test if the switch correctly debits Byte ACi and accepts frames when Byte ACi is greater than the frame size.

rules.name: Frame-based Frame Acceptance

constraint.value: If Frame ACi is greater than S i max, the frame is accepted and Frame ACi is debited by S i max

rules.source_quote: If Frame ACi is greater than S i max, the frame is accepted and Frame ACi is debited by S i max
rules.test_hint: Send frames to test if the switch correctly debits Frame ACi and accepts frames when Frame ACi is greater than S i max.

rules.name: Frame Check Sequence Validation

constraint.value: The switch should discard Frames that do not satisfy the CRC test

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard Frames that do not satisfy this test.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect CRC values to ensure they are discarded by the switch.

rules.name: Ethernet Frame Size Validation
rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming Ethernet frames having an Ethernet frame size (L) greater than 1518 or less than 64 bytes.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sizes outside the 64-1518 byte range to ensure they are discarded by the switch.

rules.name: Discard frames with non-integral octet size

constraint.value: Frame size must be an integral number of octets

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames having an Ethernet frame size that is not an integral number of octets (alignment errors).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sizes that are not whole octets to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Discard frames exceeding maximum size

constraint.value: greater than Lmax

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is greater than the maximum size (Lmax) allowed for the relevant VL.
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than the configured Lmax for a VL to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Discard frames smaller than minimum size

constraint.value: less than Smin

rules.source_quote: The switch should also discard incoming frames which total Ethernet line size is smaller than the minimum size (Smin) allowed for the relevant VL.
rules.test_hint: Send frames smaller than the configured Smin for a VL to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Discard frames with erroneous MAC destination address

constraint.value: MAC destination address must have a correct 32-bit constant field

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames with a MAC destination address that has an erroneous 32-bit constant field.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with incorrect MAC destination address fields to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Discard frames with disallowed VL ID

constraint.value: VL id must be allowed on the incoming port

rules.source_quote: The switch should discard incoming frames for which the VL id is not allowed on the incoming port.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with VL IDs not allowed on the port to test if they are discarded.

rules.name: Configure BAG values
rules.source_quote: The Traffic Policing function of the Switch should at least be configurable for BAG values in the range 1ms to 128 ms.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure BAG values outside the specified range to test if they are rejected.

rules.name: Configure maximum Jitter values
rules.source_quote: The traffic policing function should at a minimum be configurable for maximum allowed Jitter values in the range 0 to 10 milliseconds.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure Jitter values outside the specified range to test if they are rejected.

rules.name: Handle Ethernet frame sizes
rules.source_quote: The traffic policing function should be able to handle at least Ethernet frames sizes (L) in the range [64-1518] octets.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with sizes outside the specified range to test if they are handled correctly.

rules.name: Policing resolution

constraint.value: less than or equal to 100

rules.source_quote: Traffic should be policed with a resolution of less than or equal to 100 μs.

rules.name: Maintain VL Frame Order

constraint.value: The order of input and output frames belonging to a Virtual Link should be maintained by the switch.

rules.source_quote: The order of input and output frames belonging to a Virtual Link should be maintained by the switch.
rules.test_hint: Send frames in a specific order on a VL and check if the switch maintains the order.

rules.name: Do Not Modify Frame Check Sequence

constraint.value: The switch should not modify the Frame Check Sequence of incoming frames.

rules.source_quote: The switch should not modify the Frame Check Sequence of incoming frames.
rules.test_hint: Check if the FCS of frames is altered after passing through the switch.

rules.name: Use Destination Address for Forwarding

constraint.value: The content of the Destination Address field should be used to obtain from the configuration table the appropriate port(s) to which the frame has to be forwarded.

rules.source_quote: For each frame, the content of the Destination Address field should be used to obtain from the configuration table the appropriate port(s) to which the frame has to be forwarded.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with specific destination addresses and verify they are forwarded to the correct ports.

rules.name: Discard Frames on Buffer Congestion

constraint.value: If an output port cannot accept a frame due to buffer congestion, this frame should be discarded for this port.

rules.source_quote: If an output port cannot accept a frame due to buffer congestion, this frame should be discarded for this port.
rules.test_hint: Simulate buffer congestion and check if frames are discarded.

rules.name: Max Delay for Frame Transmission

constraint.value: An output port should not transmit frames that are older than 'max delay'.

rules.source_quote: An output port should not transmit frames that are older than 'max delay'.
rules.test_hint: Introduce delays and check if frames exceeding 'max delay' are discarded.

rules.name: Traffic Prioritization Based on MAC Address
rules.source_quote: The Switch should have a traffic prioritization mechanism based on MAC destination address with 2 traffic classes: High Priority and Low Priority.
rules.test_hint: Send mixed priority frames and verify high priority frames are sent first.

rules.name: Minimum Inter Frame Gap

constraint.value: If frames are present at the output port, switch should send them with a minimum Inter Frame Gap.

rules.source_quote: If frames are present at the output port, switch should send them with a minimum Inter Frame Gap.
rules.test_hint: Check if the switch maintains a minimum inter frame gap during transmission.

rules.name: Fault/Healthy Indicator Update Interval
rules.source_quote: The Fault/Healthy MIB variable should be updated every 100 ms (like the other MIB variables).
rules.test_hint: Generate a scenario where the Fault/Healthy indicator is not updated every 100 ms and observe if the switch detects and reports the issue.

rules.name: Fault Indicator Condition

constraint.value: Fault when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault

rules.source_quote: The Healthy/Fault indicator should be set to 'Fault' when at least one used Ethernet port is in fault.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a fault on an Ethernet port and verify if the Fault/Healthy indicator is set to 'Fault'.

rules.name: Configuration File Uniformity

constraint.value: All configuration files must be identical for all switches within a network

rules.source_quote: All files have to be identical for all switches within a network.
rules.test_hint: Introduce a discrepancy in configuration files across switches and observe if the network detects inconsistency.

rules.name: OPS Configuration File Usage
rules.source_quote: The OPS_Configuration_File, corresponding to the loadable configuration, that is used when the Switch is in Operational mode (OPS).
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use a non-OPS configuration file during operational mode and check if the switch rejects it.

rules.name: Default Configuration Table

constraint.value: Defines default behavior of the End System of the Switch

rules.source_quote: The Default_Configuration_Table is used to define the default behavior of the End System of the Switch: default reception and default transmission.
rules.test_hint: Alter the default configuration table and observe if the switch defaults to incorrect behavior.

rules.name: Default Port Speed
rules.source_quote: The default port speed should be set to 100 Mbps, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure the port speed to a value other than 100 Mbps and observe the switch behavior.

rules.name: Default Reception VL Subscription

constraint.value: The Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position).

rules.source_quote: Depending of its position in the aircraft network, acquired by pin programming, the Switch subscribes by default to one unique reception VL, further called VL (0, position).
rules.test_hint: Simulate different pin programming positions and verify if the switch subscribes to the correct default reception VL.

rules.name: Default Reception VL Characteristics

constraint.value: The reception part of the Default_Configuration_Table should contain VL identifiers, Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size, and Bandwidth Allocation Gap.

rules.source_quote: The reception part of the Default_Configuration_Table of the Switch should contain at least, in nonvolatile memory, the following information (characteristics of the default reception VL): VL identifiers (MAC destination address): VL (0,position), Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax), Bandwidth Allocation Gap.
rules.test_hint: Check if the default configuration table contains the required characteristics for the default reception VL.

rules.name: Default Transmission VL Characteristics

constraint.value: The transmission part of the Default_Configuration_Table should contain VL identifier, Bandwidth Allocation GAP, and Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size.

rules.source_quote: The transmission part of the Default_Configuration_Table of the Switch should contain at least, in non-volatile memory, the following information (characteristics of the default transmission VL): VL identifier (MAC destination address): VL (1,position), Bandwidth Allocation GAP, Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (smax).
rules.test_hint: Verify if the default configuration table contains the required characteristics for the default transmission VL.

rules.name: OPS Configuration File Consistency

constraint.value: The OPS_Configuration_File should be a field loadable software file compliant with ARINC 615A and ARINC 665.

rules.source_quote: The OPS_Configuration_File should be a field loadable software file compliant with ARINC 615A and ARINC 665.

rules.name: Bandwidth Allocation Gap

constraint.value: defined per VL

rules.source_quote: Bandwith Allocation Gap (BAGi)
rules.test_hint: Configure a VL with an incorrect BAG value to test switch handling.

rules.name: Maximum Allowed Jitter

constraint.value: defined per VL

rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Jitter
rules.test_hint: Introduce jitter beyond the allowed maximum to test switch policing.

rules.name: Maximum Ethernet Line Size

constraint.value: defined per VL

rules.source_quote: Maximum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smax)
rules.test_hint: Send frames larger than Smax to test switch frame size enforcement.

rules.name: Minimum Ethernet Line Size

constraint.value: defined per VL

rules.source_quote: Minimum allowed Total Ethernet Line size (Smin)
rules.test_hint: Send frames smaller than Smin to test switch frame size enforcement.

rules.name: INIT Mode Entry

constraint.value: Switch enters INIT mode after power rise or reset

rules.source_quote: The Switch enters the INIT mode after power rises or after a reset.

rules.name: OPS Mode Functionality

constraint.value: Switch performs operational functions in OPS mode

rules.source_quote: OPS is the operational mode of the Switch. In this mode, the Switch performs operational functions: frame and traffic filtering function, switching function, monitoring function, etc.

rules.name: Passive Mode Activation

constraint.value: Anomaly detected during INIT leads to PASSIVE MODE

rules.source_quote: Anomaly detected during the INIT mode will lead to the PASSIVE MODE activation.

rules.name: Quiet Mode Activation

constraint.value: Entered in event of catastrophic failure

rules.source_quote: QUIET mode is entered in the event of any sort of catastrophic failure that would cause the functional behavior of the switch to be questionable.

rules.name: Switch enters OPS mode

constraint.value: Switch enters OPS mode if compatibility checks are correct and shop condition is not active.

rules.source_quote: After the initialization sequence, the Switch should enter in OPS (operational mode) if the result of compatibility checks is correct and if the shop condition is not active.
rules.test_hint: Simulate incorrect compatibility checks or active shop condition to prevent OPS mode entry.

rules.name: Switch enters DL mode from INIT

constraint.value: Switch enters DL mode from INIT if Switch_Ground_Condition is active and compatibility checks are incorrect or no software is loaded.

rules.source_quote: To allow the uploading of an empty Switch... the Switch should enter in DL MODE only if the following conditions are both true: The Switch_Ground_Condition is active The results of compatibility checks are incorrect or there is no loaded software
rules.test_hint: Ensure Switch_Ground_Condition is inactive or compatibility checks are correct to prevent DL mode entry from INIT.

rules.name: Switch enters DL mode from OPS

constraint.value: Switch enters DL mode from OPS if Switch_Ground_Condition is active, ARINC 615A uploading operation initialization request is received, and header file is accepted.

rules.source_quote: From the OPS MODE, the Switch should enter the DL MODE only if the following conditions are all true: The Switch_Ground_Condition is active The Switch received an ARINC 615A uploading operation initialization request from the dataloader ([TH_Uploading_Initialization] message) addressed to the own end system of the Switch The header file has been received and accepted
rules.test_hint: Prevent DL mode entry from OPS by ensuring any of the conditions are not met.

rules.name: Switch enters PASSIVE mode

constraint.value: Switch enters PASSIVE mode if pin programming parity check fails or safety test result is incorrect.

rules.source_quote: From the INIT mode, the Switch should enter in PASSIVE Mode as soon as one of the following conditions is true: Pin programming parity check fails Safety Test (if any) result is incorrect
rules.test_hint: Simulate a failed pin programming parity check or incorrect safety test result to trigger PASSIVE mode entry.

rules.name: Switch enters QUIET mode

constraint.value: Switch enters QUIET mode in the event of catastrophic failures such as programming pin CRC failure, heart beat monitor test failure, etc.

rules.source_quote: QUIET mode is entered in the event of any sort of catastrophic failure that would cause the functional behavior of the switch to be questionable.
rules.test_hint: Simulate catastrophic failures like CRC failures or monitor test failures to trigger QUIET mode entry.

rules.name: Maximum Field Loadable Software
rules.source_quote: The Switch should not have more than two field loadable software (OPS_Configuration_File and OPS_Software).
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure a switch with more than two field loadable software files.

rules.name: Pin Programming Read Condition

constraint.value: true

rules.source_quote: Hardware program pins should be read during the initialization (INIT mode) of the SWITCH only if the Switch_Ground_Condition is true and before performing the Safety Test (if any).
rules.test_hint: Simulate a scenario where the Switch_Ground_Condition is false and verify if the switch avoids reading hardware program pins.

rules.name: Pin Programming Parity Check

constraint.value: parity check

rules.source_quote: The 12 program pins (P1 to P12) should be checked by a parity bit.
rules.test_hint: Introduce parity errors in the program pins and observe if the switch detects and handles the error.

rules.name: VL Processing Capacity
rules.source_quote: The filtering, policing, and forwarding function of the switch should be able to process at least 4096 VLs.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to configure more than 4096 VLs and observe if the switch can still process them.

rules.name: Port Speed Configuration
rules.source_quote: Each port speed should be configurable to operate to speeds of 10 Mbps or 100Mps in full duplex, without auto negotiation.
rules.test_hint: Configure a port with a speed outside the allowed values and observe the behavior.

rules.name: Wire Speed Frame Processing

constraint.value: wire speed

rules.source_quote: The switch must be able to process (i.e. receive, filter, police, relay, transmit) all frames that are incoming at wire speed whatever their size.
rules.test_hint: Send frames at wire speed and observe if the switch can process them without dropping.

rules.name: Technological Latency Limit

constraint.value: less than 100

rules.source_quote: The technological latency of the switch should be less than 100 μs.
rules.test_hint: Introduce artificial delays in the switch processing to exceed 100 μs latency.

rules.name: Minimum Buffer Capacity

constraint.value: at least 512

rules.source_quote: Each output port of the switch should be able to buffer at least 512 frames (balanced between high and low priority).
rules.test_hint: Send a burst of frames exceeding 512 to test buffer overflow handling.

rules.name: Performance Measurement

constraint.value: 100 x (1 / (last_frame_latency - technological_latency + 1))

rules.source_quote: The performance (as a percentage of wire-speed capability) is given by the formula: Performance = 100 x (1 / (last_frame_latency - technological_latency + 1))

rules.name: Ethernet Big Endian Byte Order
rules.source_quote: An aircraft data network for byte order, like the internet standard, specifies that integers are sent with the most significant byte first (i.e., Big Endian style).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with integers encoded in Little Endian and observe if the network correctly identifies the error.

rules.name: Ethernet Bit Order in Transmission

constraint.value: Most significant bit is transmitted first

rules.source_quote: Bit 24 is the first bit on the medium, bit 7 is the last bit on the medium for this long integer.
rules.test_hint: Transmit frames with bits in reverse order and check if the network processes them incorrectly.

rules.name: Transfer Syntax Translation

constraint.value: Messages must be translated to and from the transfer syntax at the network interface and destination computers.

rules.source_quote: The underlying platform (computer and network interface) may perform a translation of the message to the transfer syntax. The message is forwarded through the network to one or more destination computers where another translation is performed from the transfer syntax to the abstract syntax before the message is passed to the applications.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send messages without translating to the correct transfer syntax to see if the network correctly identifies and handles the error.

rules.name: Use of Defined Data Primitives
rules.source_quote: Every effort should be made to use only the data primitives listed in Table 1-1.0 for AFDX networks.
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could introduce data elements not listed in the defined data primitives to test if the network rejects or mishandles them.

rules.name: Signed 32-bit Integer Range
rules.source_quote: Signed_32 Integer 32 -231 ... 231 - 1
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send a Signed_32 integer outside of this range to test if the network enforces the range constraint.

rules.name: Signed 64-bit Integer Range
rules.source_quote: Signed_64 Integer 64 -263 … 263 - 1
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send a Signed_64 integer outside of this range to test if the network enforces the range constraint.

rules.name: Float 32-bit Range
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send a Float_32 value outside of this range to test if the network enforces the range constraint.

rules.name: Float 64-bit Range
rules.test_hint: A fuzzer could send a Float_64 value outside of this range to test if the network enforces the range constraint.

rules.name: 32-bit Signed Integer Representation

constraint.value: 32-bit two's complement

rules.source_quote: The 32-bit signed integer uses the two’s complement data representation format.

rules.name: 64-bit Signed Integer Representation

constraint.value: 64-bit two's complement

rules.source_quote: The 64-bit signed integer uses the two’s complement data representation as shown in Figure 1-2.2.

rules.name: 32-bit Floating Point Representation

constraint.value: IEEE 754 single precision

rules.source_quote: The single precision floating point format is 32 bits long with 3 fields.
rules.source_section: 1-2.3.1 Standard Precision Floating Point – Float_32 - IEEE 754

rules.name: 64-bit Floating Point Representation

constraint.value: IEEE 754 double precision

rules.source_quote: The double precision floating point format is 64 bits long with 3 fields.
rules.source_section: 1-2.3.2 Double Precision Floating Point – Float_64 - IEEE 754

rules.name: Boolean Representation

constraint.value: Single bit in a 32-bit field

rules.source_quote: Booleans are represented by a single bit in a 32-bit field.

rules.name: Boolean Packing in 32-bit Structure

constraint.value: Booleans must be packed into 32-bit structures, starting from the least significant bit. Unused bits at the most significant end must be all binary zeros.

rules.source_quote: Booleans are assigned to a structure starting from the least significant bit and filling in toward the most significant bit. Unused bits at the most significant end of the 32-bit structure must be all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Generate frames with Boolean data packed incorrectly, such as starting from the most significant bit or leaving non-zero bits in unused positions.

rules.name: String Length Field

constraint.value: The first 2 bytes of the string structure must be a 16-bit unsigned integer representing the length of the string.

rules.source_quote: The first 2 bytes of the string structure is a 16-bit unsigned integer, this value is the length of the string (number of characters in the string).
rules.test_hint: Create frames with incorrect string length fields, such as a length that does not match the actual number of characters.

rules.name: Unused Bytes in Opaque Data

constraint.value: All unused bytes of an opaque data structure should be filled with binary zeros.

rules.source_quote: All unused bytes of an opaque data structure should be filled with binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with opaque data structures that have non-zero values in unused bytes.

rules.name: Variable Length Opaque Data Length Field

constraint.value: The length field is a 16-bit unsigned integer that defines how many bytes the data field occupies.

rules.source_quote: The variable length opaque data structure is defined as a half word (16 bits) length field followed by a sequence of n bytes numbered 1 through n.
rules.test_hint: Craft frames with variable length opaque data where the length field does not match the actual number of bytes in the data field.

rules.name: Implicit Message Format

constraint.value: Implicit messages contain only data parameters with no format overhead. The message format is known by the port number it is received on.

rules.source_quote: Implicit messages have no format overhead associated with them. The message contains only the data parameters with no means of identifying how the message content is to be interpreted.
rules.test_hint: Send implicit messages with additional format overhead or incorrect port numbers, violating the implicit message structure.

rules.name: Allowed Port Number Range
rules.source_quote: Transport layer port assignments are therefore not critical and can be assigned by a system integrator using any values in the range 1 to 65535.
rules.test_hint: Generate traffic using port numbers outside the range 1 to 65535 to test network behavior.

rules.name: Data Element Alignment

constraint.value: Data element address must be evenly divisible by its length in bytes.

rules.source_quote: A data element is said to be aligned if the address of the element in memory is evenly divisible by the data element length (in bytes).
rules.test_hint: Send frames with misaligned data elements to test if the network correctly identifies and handles alignment issues.

rules.name: Reserved Word Alignment

constraint.value: Reserved word must be aligned on a 32-bit boundary.

rules.source_quote: The Reserved word at the beginning of the message should be aligned on a 32-bit boundary.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with the reserved word misaligned to test if the network detects and handles the misalignment.

rules.name: Functional Status Sets Alignment

constraint.value: Functional Status Sets should be aligned on 32-bit boundaries.

rules.source_quote: Functional Status Sets should also be aligned on 32-bit boundaries throughout the message.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with misaligned Functional Status Sets to test if the network identifies and handles alignment issues.

rules.name: Functional Status Set Structure

constraint.value: The Functional Status Set is a 32-bit field made up of four 8-bit status fields. Each status field represents the health and status of a Data Set.

rules.source_quote: The Functional Status Set (FSS) is a 32-bit field made up of four 8 bit status fields (see Figure 3.4.2).
rules.test_hint: Create a message with an incorrect number of status fields in the Functional Status Set and observe if the network detects the anomaly.

rules.name: Functional Status Value Handling
rules.source_quote: If a receiver reads a functional status value other than 0,3,12, or 48, it will discard the data in the associated DS.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with functional status values outside the allowed set (e.g., 1, 2, 4) and check if the receiver discards the data.

rules.name: Spare Field Placement

constraint.value: Spare data fields can only be placed at the end of the DS.

rules.source_quote: Spare data fields can only be placed at the end of the DS.
rules.test_hint: Create data sets with spare fields not at the end and observe if the network handles them correctly.

rules.name: Unused Spare Field Content

constraint.value: binary zeros

rules.source_quote: Spare data fields should be filled in with binary zeros if unused.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with unused spare fields filled with non-zero values and observe if the network processes them correctly.

rules.name: Reserved Field Content

constraint.value: binary zeros

rules.source_quote: The 32-bit reserved field should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Send frames with the reserved field filled with non-zero values and observe if the network processes them correctly.

rules.name: Global Spare Field Content

constraint.value: binary zeros

rules.source_quote: If this field is included in a message, it should be filled with all binary zeros.
rules.test_hint: Include a global spare field in frames and fill it with non-zero values to test if the network processes them correctly.

rules.name: Minimum Ethernet Payload Size
rules.source_quote: The minimum size packet in Ethernet has a payload of 18 bytes. If a message is sent on an AFDX network that is less than 18 bytes long the message will be padded out to 18 bytes before it appears on the medium.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with a payload smaller than 18 bytes and check if it is padded to 18 bytes before transmission.

rules.name: Avoid Shifting Parameters

constraint.value: When removing a parameter, replace it with a pad and do not shift remaining parameters.

rules.source_quote: When removing a parameter from a data set, replace it with a pad. Do not shift the remainder of the message up and remove the place the parameter was filling.
rules.test_hint: Remove a parameter from a data set and verify that the remaining parameters are not shifted, but the space is padded instead.

rules.name: Efficient Use of Network

constraint.value: Network becomes more efficient with packet sizes in the hundreds of bytes.

rules.source_quote: Sending 18-byte payloads is not an efficient use of the network since this payload is small compared to the overhead of the packets. The network starts to become more efficient when packet sizes get up into the hundreds of bytes long.

rules.name: Packed Boolean Right Justification

constraint.value: Packed Booleans are right justified, filling bits from right to left with spare on the left.

rules.source_quote: Packed Booleans are right justified, they begin filling in bits from right to left with spare on the left.
rules.test_hint: Create a frame with a Boolean data primitive that is not right justified to test how the network handles misaligned Boolean data.

rules.name: Interpretation of NOT APPLICABLE
rules.source_quote: NOT APPLICABLE should be interpreted as MUST NOT.
rules.source_section: Attachment 2 - IP/ICMP, UDP, AND TCP PROFILE PROVISIONS
rules.test_hint: Attempt to use a feature marked as NOT APPLICABLE to verify that the network enforces it as MUST NOT.

rules.name: Window size as unsigned number

constraint.value: unsigned

rules.source_quote: The window size MUST be treated as an unsigned number.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with a negative window size to test if the network treats it as unsigned.

rules.name: Probing zero windows

constraint.value: MUST be supported

rules.source_quote: Probing of zero (offered) windows MUST be supported.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a zero window condition and check if probes are sent.

rules.name: Urgent pointer points to last octet

constraint.value: points to last octet

rules.source_quote: The urgent pointer points to the sequence number of the LAST octet (not LAST+1).
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with the urgent pointer set to LAST+1 and observe the network's response.

rules.name: Receive TCP option in any segment

constraint.value: MUST be able to receive

rules.source_quote: A TCP MUST be able to receive a TCP option in any segment.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP options in various segments to check if they are processed correctly.

rules.name: Sender computes checksum

constraint.value: MUST generate

rules.source_quote: The sender MUST generate.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame without a checksum to test if the network detects the error.

rules.name: Reject multicast or broadcast IP address on OPEN

constraint.value: MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address).

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Attempt to open a connection using a broadcast or multicast IP address and verify that it is rejected.

rules.name: Silently discard SYN to broadcast/multicast address

constraint.value: MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.
rules.test_hint: Send a SYN segment to a broadcast or multicast address and verify that it is silently discarded.

rules.name: TIME-WAIT state duration

constraint.value: 2xMSL

rules.source_quote: When a connection is closed actively, it MUST linger in TIME-WAIT state for a time 2xMSL.
rules.test_hint: Close a connection actively and verify that it remains in TIME-WAIT state for twice the Maximum Segment Lifetime (MSL).

rules.name: Implement Karn's and Jacobson's algorithms

constraint.value: MUST implement Karn's algorithm and Jacobson's algorithm for computing the retransmission timeout (RTO).

rules.source_quote: A host TCP MUST implement Karn's algorithm and Jacobson's algorithm for computing the retransmission timeout (RTO).

rules.name: Exponential backoff for RTO

constraint.value: MUST include exponential backoff for successive RTO values for the same segment.

rules.source_quote: This implementation also MUST include 'exponential backoff' for successive RTO values for the same segment.

rules.name: Retransmission of SYN segments

constraint.value: Retransmission of SYN segments should use the same algorithm as data segments

rules.source_quote: Retransmission of SYN segments SHOULD use the same algorithm as data segments.
rules.test_hint: Generate SYN segments and observe if retransmission follows the same algorithm as data segments.

rules.name: Initial RTO value
rules.source_quote: (b) RTO = 3 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Set initial RTO to a value other than 3 seconds and observe behavior.

rules.name: Upper bound on RTO
rules.source_quote: The upper bound should be 2*MSL, i.e., 240 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Set RTO upper bound to a value greater than 240 seconds and observe behavior.

rules.name: Delayed ACK maximum delay
rules.source_quote: The delay MUST be less than 0.5 seconds.
rules.test_hint: Delay ACKs for more than 0.5 seconds and observe if the network reacts.

rules.name: Nagle Algorithm
rules.source_quote: A TCP SHOULD implement the Nagle Algorithm [TCP:9] to coalesce short segments.
rules.test_hint: Disable Nagle Algorithm and send short segments to see if they are coalesced.

rules.name: Close connection on R2 retransmissions

constraint.value: greater than R1

rules.source_quote: When the number of transmissions of the same segment reaches a threshold R2 greater than R1, close the connection.
rules.test_hint: Set R2 to a value less than or equal to R1 and observe if the connection closes prematurely.

rules.name: SYN retransmission duration

constraint.value: at least 3 minutes

rules.source_quote: R2 for a SYN segment MUST be set large enough to provide retransmission of the segment for at least 3 minutes.
rules.test_hint: Set R2 for SYN segments to less than 3 minutes and observe if retransmissions stop prematurely.

rules.name: Keep-alive default state
rules.source_quote: If keep-alives are included, they MUST default to off.
rules.test_hint: Send a TCP connection with keep-alives enabled by default to see if the network rejects or logs the violation.

rules.name: Keep-alive interval configurability

constraint.value: >= 2 hours

rules.source_quote: Default is at least 2 hours
rules.test_hint: Configure a keep-alive interval less than 2 hours and observe if the network accepts it.

rules.name: Ignore unknown TCP options

constraint.value: TCP MUST ignore options that it does not understand.

rules.source_quote: TCP MUST ignore options that it does not understand.
rules.test_hint: Send TCP segments with unknown options and check if they are ignored.

rules.name: Source Quench reaction

constraint.value: TCP MUST react to a Source Quench by slowing transmission.

rules.source_quote: TCP MUST react to a Source Quench by slowing transmission on the connection.
rules.test_hint: Send a Source Quench message and observe if the TCP connection slows down.

rules.name: Reject invalid IP address on OPEN

constraint.value: MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address.

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST reject as an error a local OPEN call for an invalid remote IP address.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to open a TCP connection to an invalid IP address and check for rejection.

rules.name: Discard SYN to broadcast/multicast

constraint.value: MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.

rules.source_quote: A TCP implementation MUST silently discard an incoming SYN segment that is addressed to a broadcast or multicast address.
rules.test_hint: Send a SYN segment to a broadcast or multicast address and verify it is discarded.

rules.name: ICMP Port Unreachable Handling

constraint.value: UDP SHOULD send an ICMP Port Unreachable message if a datagram arrives addressed to a UDP port for which there is no pending LISTEN call.

rules.source_quote: If a datagram arrives addressed to a UDP port for which there is no pending LISTEN call, UDP SHOULD send an ICMP Port Unreachable message.
rules.test_hint: Send a UDP datagram to a port with no LISTEN call and check if an ICMP Port Unreachable message is generated.

rules.name: Discard Datagram with Invalid Checksum

constraint.value: If a UDP datagram is received with a checksum that is non-zero and invalid, UDP MUST silently discard the datagram.

rules.source_quote: If a UDP datagram is received with a checksum that is non-zero and invalid, UDP MUST silently discard the datagram.
rules.test_hint: Send a UDP datagram with an invalid checksum and verify that it is silently discarded.

rules.name: Discard Datagram with Invalid IP Source Address

constraint.value: A UDP datagram received with an invalid IP source address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address) must be discarded by UDP or by the IP layer.

rules.source_quote: A UDP datagram received with an invalid IP source address (e.g., a broadcast or multicast address) must be discarded by UDP or by the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Send a UDP datagram with a broadcast or multicast source address and verify that it is discarded.

rules.name: Silently discard datagram with non-IP version 4
rules.source_quote: A datagram whose version number is not 4 MUST be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with an IP version number other than 4 and check if it is discarded.

rules.name: Verify IP checksum and discard bad datagram

constraint.value: Verify checksum and discard if incorrect

rules.source_quote: A host MUST verify the IP header checksum on every received datagram and silently discard every datagram that has a bad checksum.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with an incorrect IP checksum and check if it is discarded.

rules.name: Source address must be host's own IP address

constraint.value: Source address must be one of host's own IP addresses

rules.source_quote: When a host sends any datagram, the IP source address MUST be one of its own IP addresses (but not a broadcast or multicast address).
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with a source IP address that is not assigned to the host and check if it is rejected.

rules.name: Silently discard datagram with bad destination address

constraint.value: Discard if destination address is not for the host

rules.source_quote: A host MUST silently discard an incoming datagram that is not destined for the host.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with a destination address that does not match the host and check if it is discarded.

rules.name: Discard received packets with TTL < 2

constraint.value: TTL >= 2

rules.source_quote: Discard received packets with TTL < 2
rules.test_hint: Send a packet with TTL less than 2 and check if it is discarded.

rules.name: IP Options Specification

constraint.value: There must be a means for the transport layer to specify IP options to be included in transmitted IP datagrams.

rules.source_quote: There MUST be a means for the transport layer to specify IP options to be included in transmitted IP datagrams.
rules.test_hint: Try to send a datagram with IP options specified and observe if they are included in the transmitted datagram.

rules.name: Support Source Route Options

constraint.value: A host must support originating a source route and must be able to act as the final destination of a source route.

rules.source_quote: A host MUST support originating a source route and MUST be able to act as the final destination of a source route.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send and receive datagrams with source route options and observe if the host processes them correctly.

rules.name: Silently Discard Unknown ICMP Types

constraint.value: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it must be silently discarded.

rules.source_quote: If an ICMP message of unknown type is received, it MUST be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send an ICMP message with an unknown type and check if it is discarded without any response.

rules.name: ICMP Error Message Content

constraint.value: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error.

rules.source_quote: Every ICMP error message includes the Internet header and at least the first 8 data octets of the datagram that triggered the error; more than 8 octets MAY be sent.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram that triggers an ICMP error and verify the content of the returned ICMP error message.

rules.name: No ICMP error messages
rules.source_quote: Return ICMP error messages (when not prohibited) 3.2.2  X  No ICMP errors
rules.test_hint: Send a frame that would typically generate an ICMP error message and verify that no ICMP error is returned.

rules.name: No ICMP redirect from End Systems
rules.source_quote: Host send Redirect 3.2.2.2  X  No ICMP redirect from ES
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send an ICMP Redirect message from an End System and ensure it is not sent.

rules.name: No Source Quench messages
rules.source_quote: Send Source Quench if buffering exceeded 3.2.2.3   X
rules.test_hint: Simulate buffer exhaustion and verify that no ICMP Source Quench message is sent.

rules.name: No Parameter Problem messages
rules.source_quote: Send parameter Problem messages 3.2.2.5  X  Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with a parameter problem and ensure that no ICMP Parameter Problem message is generated.

rules.name: ICMP Echo Server Requirement

constraint.value: Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.

rules.source_quote: Every host MUST implement an ICMP Echo server function that receives Echo Requests and sends corresponding Echo Replies.
rules.test_hint: Test by sending an ICMP Echo Request and verifying that an Echo Reply is sent back by the host.

rules.name: Echo Request to Broadcast/Multicast

constraint.value: An ICMP Echo Request destined to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded.

rules.source_quote: An ICMP Echo Request destined to an IP broadcast or IP multicast address MAY be silently discarded.
rules.test_hint: Send an ICMP Echo Request to a broadcast or multicast address and check if it is discarded.

rules.name: Echo Reply Source Address

constraint.value: The IP source address in an ICMP Echo Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding ICMP Echo Request message.

rules.source_quote: The IP source address in an ICMP Echo Reply MUST be the same as the specific-destination address of the corresponding ICMP Echo Request message.
rules.test_hint: Verify that the source address of an Echo Reply matches the destination address of the original Echo Request.

rules.name: Echo Reply Data Integrity

constraint.value: Data received in an ICMP Echo Request MUST be entirely included in the resulting Echo Reply.

rules.source_quote: Data received in an ICMP Echo Request MUST be entirely included in the resulting Echo Reply.
rules.test_hint: Send an Echo Request with specific data and verify that the Echo Reply contains the same data.

rules.name: Pass Echo Reply to Higher Layer

constraint.value: Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface, unless the corresponding Echo Request originated in the IP layer.

rules.source_quote: Echo Reply messages MUST be passed to the ICMP user interface, unless the corresponding Echo Request originated in the IP layer.
rules.test_hint: Verify that Echo Replies are correctly passed to the ICMP user interface.

rules.name: Allowed ICMP Messages
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages other than 'echo request' or 'echo reply' and observe if they are processed or rejected.

rules.name: Unauthorized Address Mask Reply
rules.source_quote: A system MUST NOT send an Address Mask Reply unless it is an authoritative agent for address masks.
rules.test_hint: Send an Address Mask Reply from a non-authoritative agent and check if the network accepts or rejects it.

rules.name: Broadcast Address Mask Reply

constraint.value: If configured as an agent, the host must broadcast an Address Mask Reply on initialization.

rules.source_quote: If it is configured as an agent, the host MUST broadcast an Address Mask Reply for the mask on the appropriate interface when it initializes.
rules.test_hint: Configure a host as an authoritative agent and check if it broadcasts an Address Mask Reply upon initialization.

rules.name: Static Routing Definition

constraint.value: AFDX networks are statically defined and do not use dynamic routing or default gateways.

rules.source_quote: AFDX is statically defined, no default gateways

rules.name: ICMP Echo Handling
rules.source_quote: Only ICMP "echo request" and "echo reply" are allowed.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages other than echo request/reply and observe if they are processed or rejected.

rules.name: Reassemble Incoming Datagrams
rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST implement reassembly of IP datagrams.
rules.test_hint: Send fragmented datagrams to test if the IP layer reassembles them correctly.

rules.name: Minimum Datagram Size for Reassembly
rules.source_quote: EMTU_R MUST be greater than or equal to 576.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to reassemble datagrams smaller than 576 bytes to check for compliance.

rules.name: Send ICMP Time Exceeded on Reassembly Timeout

constraint.value: Send ICMP Time Exceeded if reassembly timeout occurs and fragment zero is received

rules.source_quote: If this timeout expires, the partially-reassembled datagram MUST be discarded and an ICMP Time Exceeded message sent to the source host (if fragment zero has been received).
rules.test_hint: Induce a reassembly timeout and check if an ICMP Time Exceeded message is sent.

rules.name: Local Fragmentation of Outgoing Packets
rules.source_quote: A host that does not implement local fragmentation MUST ensure that the transport layer (for TCP) or the application layer (for UDP) obtains MMS_S from the IP layer and does not send a datagram exceeding MMS_S in size.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send datagrams exceeding MMS_S without local fragmentation.

rules.name: Reply with Same Address as Specified Destination Address

constraint.value: Source address for response should be the specific-destination address of the request

rules.source_quote: If the datagram is sent in response to a received datagram, the source address for the response SHOULD be the specific-destination address of the request.
rules.test_hint: Send requests and verify if responses use the specified destination address as the source.

rules.name: Silently Discard Datagram in Wrong Interface

constraint.value: Silently discard incoming datagram if destination address does not match the receiving interface

rules.source_quote: A host MAY silently discard an incoming datagram whose destination address does not correspond to the physical interface through which it is received.
rules.test_hint: Send datagrams to incorrect interfaces and check if they are discarded.

rules.name: Source-routed datagram forwarding

constraint.value: A host may act as an intermediate hop in a source route, forwarding a source-routed datagram to the next specified hop.

rules.source_quote: Subject to restrictions given below, a host MAY be able to act as an intermediate hop in a source route, forwarding a source-routed datagram to the next specified hop.
rules.test_hint: Generate a source-routed datagram and verify if the host forwards it as an intermediate hop.

rules.name: TTL decrement on forwarding

constraint.value: The TTL field must be decremented when forwarding source-routed datagrams.

rules.source_quote: The TTL field MUST be decremented and the datagram.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with a specific TTL and check if it is decremented upon forwarding.
