rules.name: Generate ICMP Destination Unreachable
rules.source_quote: A host MUST be able to generate Destination Unreachable messages with the following codes: 4 (Fragmentation Required but DF Set) when a source-routed datagram cannot be fragmented to fit into the target network 5 (Source Route Failed) when a source-routed datagram cannot be forwarded, e.g., because of a routing problem or because the next hop of a strict source route is not on a connected network.
rules.test_hint: Send a source-routed datagram that cannot be forwarded and check if the appropriate ICMP error message is generated.

rules.name: Non-local source address in forwarding

constraint.value: A source-routed datagram being forwarded may have a source address that is not one of the IP addresses of the forwarding host.

rules.source_quote: A source-routed datagram being forwarded MAY (and normally will) have a source address that is not one of the IP addresses of the forwarding host.
rules.test_hint: Send a source-routed datagram with a non-local source address and check if it is forwarded.

rules.name: Update Record Route option

constraint.value: A host that is forwarding a source-routed datagram containing a Record Route option must update that option, if it has room.

rules.source_quote: A host that is forwarding a source-routed datagram containing a Record Route option MUST update that option, if it has room.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with a Record Route option and check if it is updated upon forwarding.

rules.name: Update Timestamp option

constraint.value: A host that is forwarding a source-routed datagram containing a Timestamp Option must add the current timestamp to that option.

rules.source_quote: A host that is forwarding a source-routed datagram containing a Timestamp Option MUST add the current timestamp to that option, according to the rules for this option.
rules.test_hint: Send a datagram with a Timestamp option and verify if the current timestamp is added upon forwarding.

rules.name: Configurable switch for non-local Source Routing

constraint.value: must default to disabled

rules.source_quote: ...and this switch MUST default to disabled.
rules.test_hint: Check if the non-local source routing switch is disabled by default.

rules.name: Recognize standard broadcast address forms
rules.source_quote: A host MUST recognize any of these forms in the destination address of an incoming datagram.
rules.test_hint: Send datagrams with different standard broadcast address forms and verify recognition.

rules.name: Support Local IP Multicasting

constraint.value: SHOULD support

rules.source_quote: A host SHOULD support local IP multicasting on all connected networks for which a mapping from Class D IP addresses to link-layer addresses has been specified.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send and receive multicast datagrams on a network and verify support.

rules.name: Join All-Hosts Group

constraint.value: SHOULD join at startup

rules.source_quote: If IGMP is not implemented, a host SHOULD still join the 'all-hosts' group (224.0.0.1) when the IP layer is initialized and remain a member for as long as the IP layer is active.
rules.test_hint: Check if the host joins the all-hosts group at IP layer initialization without IGMP.

rules.name: Pass IP Options to Transport Layer

constraint.value: MUST pass all IP options to the transport layer

rules.source_quote: The parameter opt contains all the IP options received in the datagram; these MUST also be passed to the transport layer.
rules.test_hint: Verify that all IP options in a received datagram are passed to the transport layer.

rules.name: Pass ICMP Messages to Transport Layer

constraint.value: MUST pass certain ICMP messages to transport layer

rules.source_quote: The IP layer MUST pass certain ICMP messages up to the appropriate transport-layer routine.
rules.test_hint: Send ICMP messages and check if they are passed to the transport layer.

rules.name: Domain ID Coding
rules.source_quote: The Domain ID should be coded with 4 bits. The 0000 and 1111 are forbidden values. Therefore, 14 Domains ID are possible.
rules.test_hint: Use forbidden Domain ID values (0000 or 1111) in MAC/IP address construction and observe handling.

rules.name: Side ID Coding
rules.source_quote: The Side ID format should be coded with 3 bits. The 000 and 111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Use forbidden Side ID values (000 or 111) in MAC/IP address construction and observe handling.

rules.name: Location ID Coding
rules.source_quote: The Location ID format should be coded with 5 bits. The 00000 and 11111 are forbidden values.
rules.test_hint: Use forbidden Location ID values (00000 or 11111) in MAC/IP address construction and observe handling.

rules.name: Single Label Message Structure

constraint.value: A single ARINC 429 label should be placed in a fixed length 32-bit opaque data primitive for single label messages.

rules.source_quote: Figure B-1.1 is an example of how a single label would be placed in a message. This structure should be used for single label messages.
rules.test_hint: Generate a frame with a single ARINC 429 label not placed in a 32-bit opaque data primitive and observe if the network processes it correctly.

rules.name: Multiple Label Message Structure with Single DS

constraint.value: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used, and the DS status is reflected by a single FS.

rules.source_quote: If all labels are concentrated into a single Ethernet frame by a single threaded device, a single DS should be used, and the DS status is reflected by a single FS.
rules.test_hint: Create a frame with multiple labels using a single DS and check if the network correctly interprets the FS status.

rules.name: Multiple Label Message Structure with Multiple DS

constraint.value: If a concentrator device can fail partially, more than one DS should be considered, with each DS represented by its own FS.

rules.source_quote: If the concentrator device is designed in such a way that a portion of it could fail in some way that causes some labels to be invalid, but a completely legal Ethernet frame is still generated with some valid labels, more than one DS should be considered.
rules.test_hint: Simulate a partial failure in a concentrator device and ensure that multiple DS are used with individual FS statuses.

rules.name: Variable Length Opaque Structure

constraint.value: A variable length opaque structure is used when the number of ARINC 429 labels varies, with the structure's maximum size statically configured.

rules.source_quote: Since any one message the gateway sends could have a varying number of labels, a variable length data structure is required.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame with varying numbers of labels without using a variable length structure and check if the network processes it correctly.

rules.name: Length Field in Variable Length Structure

constraint.value: The gateway computes the number of bytes with good data and loads this number into the length field of the structure.

rules.source_quote: When it is time for transmission, the gateway will compute how many bytes of the static length have good data in them and load this number into the length field of the structure.
rules.test_hint: Transmit a frame with an incorrect length field value and observe if the network detects the discrepancy.

rules.name: Application Data Encapsulation

constraint.value: Application data must be encapsulated inside a UDP datagram or a TCP segment for transmission.

rules.source_quote: Application data are transmitted by encapsulation inside an UDP datagram or a TCP segment.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send application data without encapsulating it in a UDP datagram or TCP segment.

rules.name: Message Encapsulation

constraint.value: A message must be encapsulated inside an IP datagram for end-to-end transmission through the AFDX.

rules.source_quote: To be transmitted end-to-end through the AFDX, a message must be encapsulated inside an IP datagram.
rules.test_hint: Attempt to send a message without encapsulating it in an IP datagram.

rules.name: IP Datagram Fragmentation

constraint.value: If a UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it must be broken into fragments.

rules.source_quote: Whenever an UDP datagram is too long to fit in a packet, it is break in an almost arbitrary number of pieces that are placed in fragments.
rules.test_hint: Send a UDP datagram that exceeds the MTU without fragmenting it.

rules.name: IP Datagram Structure

constraint.value: An IP datagram must consist of an IP header followed by transport layer data.

rules.source_quote: An IP datagram consists of an IP header followed by transport layer data, i.e., of an IP header followed by an UDP datagram or a segment.
rules.test_hint: Construct an IP datagram without an IP header or without transport layer data.

rules.name: Frame Structure

constraint.value: A frame must consist of a MAC header followed by a packet.

rules.source_quote: A frame is the unit of transmission at Ethernet level, and consists of a MAC header followed by a packet.
rules.test_hint: Send a frame without a MAC header or without a packet.
